MetaDescription.value: From the Chicago School of Economics to pioneering social service scholarship in the U.S., the University of Chicago is known for putting forth ideas that reshape the world.

MetaKeywords.value: scholarship, academics, academic integrity, american institutes for research, scientific breakthroughs, nobel prize, presidential medal of freedom, biggest research universities, research that changed the world

value.alt: A researcher works inside the Engel Lab

text.value:
Ideas that shape our world

UChicago research, fueled by the freedom to challenge assumptions and follow ideas where they lead, defines new fields of study and helps solve age-old problems. From medicine to quantum, and economics to climate policy, UChicago scholars and students are making foundational advances in research and achieving breakthroughs that benefit our world.

description.value: Through their foundational research, UChicago scholars and students create knowledge in their fields and enable new areas for discovery.

children.name: Measuring the earliest light in the universe
children.displayName: Measuring the earliest light in the universe

text.value:
Measuring the earliest light in the universe

Using the South Pole Telescope, UChicago scientists studied the cosmic microwave background to map the afterglow of the big bang.

children.name: Exploring how the humanities can advance AI research
children.displayName: Exploring how the humanities can advance AI research

text.value:
Exploring how the humanities can advance AI research

UChicago scholars are examining the opportunities of generative AI models provide across disciplines—and what they can reveal about knowledge and creativity.

Understanding how children’s language forms 

When does a child start building words rather than parroting them? UChicago linguistics, psychologists and computational scientists sought to find out.

Explaining how brain cells connect

UChicago scientists built a simple model to examine how brain cells organize and cluster together in a variety of organisms.

jss-single-col-wide.dataSource: /sitecore/content/UChicago Tenant/www/Home/Research and Scholarship/Data/Headline Bar Research that protects our health

description.value: From advancing cancer immunotherapy to developing new treatments that target disease at the molecular level—our medical breakthroughs are impacting lives.

jss-single-col-wide.dataSource: /sitecore/content/UChicago Tenant/www/Home/Research and Scholarship/Data/Protects Our Health Examples

children.name: Inventing a pacemaker powered by light
children.displayName: Inventing a pacemaker powered by light

text.value:
Inventing a pacemaker powered by light

UChicago researchers have created a featherlight, wireless implant that uses light to regulate heart or nerve activity, potentially replacing pacemakers.

Harnessing the body’s cancer-fighting powers

UChicago scientists are using cancer immunotherapy to treat patients for leukemia and lymphoma.

Tackling research on disease

Leveraging unique opportunities to work in UChicago labs, College students drive innovation in fields including neuroscience, bioengineering and cancer therapy.

Recycling and reusing fresh water

UChicago scientists are leading a ‘moonshot’ initiative to remove dangerous chemicals from the Great Lakes.

children.name: Unlocking the secrets of the gut microbiome
children.displayName: Unlocking the secrets of the gut microbiome

text.value:
Unlocking the secrets of the gut microbiome

UChicago researchers are working to understand the role that bacteria in our gut play in our health—and how they may impact diseases and allergies.

jss-single-col-wide.dataSource: /sitecore/content/UChicago Tenant/www/Home/Research and Scholarship/Data/Headline Bar Research that reshapes society

description.value: Breakthrough scholarship at UChicago has not only changed the way we think and view the world, but has benefitted society in fundamental ways.

children.name: Addressing complex problems in cities and schools
children.displayName: Addressing complex problems in cities and schools

text.value:
Addressing complex problems in cities and schools

The UChicago Urban Labs use academic research to inform effective policy-making to help limit crime and improve education across the country.

children.name: Measuring air pollutions impact on life expectancy
children.displayName: Measuring air pollutions impact on life expectancy

text.value:
Measuring air pollution’s impact on life expectancy

UChicago research in Asia and Africa found the risk to our health is comparable to smoking

value.alt: Air pollution from a construction site

children.name: Understanding how parents decisions shapes their kids
children.displayName: Understanding how parents decisions shapes their kids

text.value:
Understanding how parents’ decisions shapes their kids

UChicago scholars have measured the impact of choices within families—from reading at bedtime to showing affection to allowing screentime.

children.name: Examining the benefits and risks of climate systems engineering
children.displayName: Examining the benefits and risks of climate systems engineering

text.value:
Examining the benefits and risks of climate systems engineering

UChicago scholars are researching the science and policy implications of climate systems engineering, to better understand the technology while educating students and society about a warming planet.

children.name: Measuring how preschool benefits generations of families
children.displayName: Measuring how preschool benefits generations of families

text.value:
Measuring how preschool benefits generations of families

Nobel Prize-winning economist James Heckman’s decades of research found the benefits of early education on social mobility and poverty.

value.alt: A father plays with his toddler

description.value: Discovery at UChicago is actively focused on solving problems, while developing and employing new techniques and innovative technology.

jss-single-col-wide.dataSource: /sitecore/content/UChicago Tenant/www/Home/Research and Scholarship/Data/Drives Innovation Examples Carousel

children.name: Advancing work toward a secure quantum internet
children.displayName: Advancing work toward a secure quantum internet

text.value:
Advancing work toward a secure quantum internet

A 124-mile quantum network built in Chicago is one of the country’s first testbeds for quantum security technology.

children.name: Restoring touch to people with prosthetics
children.displayName: Restoring touch to people with prosthetics

text.value:
Restoring touch to people with prosthetics

By placing tiny electrodes in parts of the brain responsible for moving and feeling, UChicago scientists have created more responsive prosthetic limbs.

Designing the next generation of batteries

Engineers are developing batteries that eliminate 'forever chemicals,' such as PFAS, by using safer materials and new manufacturing techniques.

children.name: Developing tools to protect against AI piracy
children.displayName: Developing tools to protect against AI piracy

text.value:
Developing tools to protect against AI piracy

Software developed by UChicago computer scientists deliver a ‘poison pill’ to generative AI tools to protest artists' work from plagiarism.

description.value: We turn groundbreaking research into new businesses. UChicago has helped entrepreneurs take big ideas—from new cancer treatments to green energy solutions—from the labs to the real world. Through the Polsky Center’s world-renowned New Venture Challenge, more than 370 startups have been launched, including Grubhub, Braintree/Venmo and Simple Mills.

description.value: UChicago faculty have played an influential role in shaping the U.S. economy, through their insights on financial policy or their work as economic advisors to presidents. Their breakthroughs in medicine have led to new cures, startups and industry partnerships—and their research in partnership with Argonne and Fermilab national laboratories have large-scale economic impact. Studies have shown that every $1 spent by the NIH generates $2.56 of economic activity.
